rationales: Plastids mainly perform functions such as photosynthesis and storage, not aerobic respiration.
Mitochondria are the main sites of aerobic respiration in cells.
The nucleus contains genetic material and does not serve as the site of aerobic respiration.
Ribosomes synthesize proteins rather than carry out aerobic respiration.
Albumin is a protein, not the most common substance in plant cell walls.
Lignin occurs in some plant cell walls but is not their most common chemical component.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls and arthropod exoskeletons, not commonly in plant cell walls.
Cellulose is the principal and most common chemical in plant cell walls.
G1 is mainly a period of cell growth and normal metabolic activity.
S phase is when DNA is replicated.
M phase is when the cell undergoes mitosis and division.
G2 is when the cell prepares for mitosis, including synthesizing needed enzymes and proteins.
Golgi is associated with the discovery of the Golgi apparatus, not meiosis.
Walther Flemming described mitosis, not the discovery of meiosis.
Oscar Hertwig is credited with discovering meiosis during his study of fertilization.
Pasteur is known for work on microorganisms and fermentation, not meiosis.
Carbohydrates can have catalytic roles, but most enzymes are not carbohydrates.
Nucleic acids include some catalytic molecules, but most enzymes are not nucleic acids.
Lipids are not the usual molecular category of enzymes.
Most enzymes are proteins, although some RNA molecules can also act as enzymes.
Energy is released when ATP’s terminal phosphate bond, a P-P bond, is broken during hydrolysis.
A C-N bond is not the bond conventionally associated with energy release from ATP.
A C-H bond is not the bond from which cells conventionally obtain energy from ATP.
A C-O bond is not the bond conventionally associated with ATP energy release.
Colon bacteria are not commonly credited with producing vitamin A for the body.
Colon bacteria are not commonly credited with producing vitamin D.
Some bacteria in the colon synthesize vitamin K.
Vitamin C is not the vitamin generally identified as being produced by colon bacteria.
An organism is a complete living individual, not the less definite level in plant organization.
Tissues are groups of similar cells and are a definite level of organization.
The organ-system level is less definite in plants because their organs are not organized into distinct systems as clearly as in animals.
Organs such as roots, stems, and leaves are recognizable, definite plant structures.
An organelle is a structure within a cell, not a group of similar cells.
A tissue is a group of similar cells organized to perform related functions.
An organ consists of different tissues working together, rather than only similar cells.
An organ system is a group of organs working together.
Experimentation tests a hypothesis and occurs after initial observations and reasoning.
A hypothesis is proposed to explain observations, so it is not the first step.
Deduction follows from a hypothesis to form a testable prediction.
Taking observations is the basic initial step of the biological method.
Aristotle made important early contributions to biology but did not introduce binomial nomenclature.
Robert Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification system.
Ernst Haeckel contributed to biological classification but did not introduce binomial nomenclature.
Carolus Linnaeus introduced and established the system of binomial nomenclature.
In prophase, chromosomes condense but sister chromatids remain joined.
In metaphase, chromosomes line up at the cell’s equator and sister chromatids remain joined.
In anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles.
In telophase, chromosomes have reached the poles and new nuclei form.
Metaphase I involves alignment of homologous chromosome pairs and is shorter than prophase I.
Telophase I is a comparatively brief stage at the end of the first meiotic division.
Anaphase I involves separation of homologous chromosomes and is not the longest stage.
Prophase I is the longest stage of meiosis because pairing and crossing over occur during it.
Amylase breaks down starch into smaller sugars.
Pepsin digests proteins, not starch.
Lipase digests fats, not starch.
Proteases digest proteins, not starch.
Carbon dioxide is a reactant used in photosynthesis, not its gaseous by-product.
Oxygen is released as a by-product of photosynthesis in the presence of sunlight.
Water is a reactant in photosynthesis and is split during the light-dependent reactions.
Glucose is a product of photosynthesis, but it is not the gaseous by-product asked for here.
